TOLEDO, Ohio – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio announced today that Murotech Ohio Corporation, an automotive component parts manufacturer with its principal place of business in St. Marys, Ohio, has agreed to pay $3,039,615, of which $1,085,577 is restitution, to resolve allegations under the False Claims Act (FCA) that it knowingly provided false information to obtain Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans and loan forgiveness.  The company is a subsidiary of Muro Corporation, located in Japan.

The PPP program was launched through the Small Business Administration (SBA) to provide eligible companies with financial support during the COVID-19 pandemic. Murotech Ohio’s first application submitted in May 2020 certified that the company had fewer than 500 employees, but in fact, it exceeded that amount when counting affiliates. A second application submitted in January of 2021 certified that it employed fewer than 300 employees, but in truth, the company employed far more when including affiliates. Murotech Ohio then applied to have both federal loans forgiven and certified on its submitted applications that the number of employees was below program limit requirements.

This settlement resolves two lawsuits filed under the whistleblower provisions of the FCA, which allows an individual, known as the “relator,” to file a complaint on behalf of the United States for false claims and share in a portion of the government’s recovery.  The whistleblower cases are captioned United States ex rel. GNGH2, Inc. v. Murotech Ohio Corporation, case number 3:24-CV-1592 and United States ex rel. Verity Investigations, LLC. v. Murotech Ohio Corporation, case number 3:24-CV-2245. As part of the settlement, relators will receive $151,980.75 each.

The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio, with assistance from the SBA’s Office of General Counsel (SBA-OGC). 

Assistant United States Attorney Angelita Cruz Bridges handled this matter for the Northern District of Ohio.

Anyone with information about allegations of PPP fraud may submit a report with the SBA Office of the Inspector General.

The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only. There has been no determination of liability.

Alexandria, Va. – Securiport Limited Liability Company (Securiport) and Alex Stewart International, LLC (ASI), have agreed to pay a combined $1,816,943 to settle civil False Claims Act  allegations arising from the submission of statements on their applications for so-called Second Draw Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans. 

The United States alleged that Securiport and ASI received Second Draw PPP loans, which were later forgiven, after submitting false statements on loan applications that they, together with affiliates, had no more than 300 employees, an eligibility requirement specific to Second Draw PPP loans. Based on that purported false statement, the United States alleged that Securiport and ASI falsely certified they were eligible. 

The settlement began with a lawsuit, United States ex rel. Verity Investigations, LLC v. Securiport Limited Liability Company, No. 1:25-cv-2027, filed under the whistleblower provision of the False Claims Act, which permits private parties to file suit on behalf of the United States for false claims presented to the federal government. The whistleblower received 10% of the government’s recovery. The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia and the U.S. Small Business Administration.

The matter was investigated by Assistant U.S. Attorney David Tannenbaum.

A copy of this press release may be found on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia. Case records may be found on PACER under case number 1:25-cv-2027. 

The civil claims settled are allegations only; there has been no determination of civil liability.

RALEIGH, N.C. – ATF Agents arrested five individuals following a federal grand jury in the Eastern District of North Carolina returning indictments alleging their involvement in a firearms trafficking scheme: four arrested in Maryland, one in Raleigh, North Carolina. This enforcement action was conducted in collaboration with the D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force, a federal task force chaired by the Homeland Security Advisor, to curb violent crime, address narcotics and firearms offenses, enforce quality-of-life and transit rules, and support local and federal police agencies. The grand jury returned a 13-count indictment charging the defendants with offenses including conspiracy to traffic firearms, firearms trafficking, and making false statements to a federally licensed firearms dealer, announced U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle and U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. 

On October 20, 2026, the Make DC Safe and Beautiful Task Force executed five federal arrest warrants related to a firearms trafficking conspiracy involving individuals who trafficked dozens of firearms from North Carolina to Washington, D.C., and the National Capital Region. The Task Force determined that co‑conspirators supplied upwards of approximately 40 firearms to individuals across multiple states, including Washington, D.C., New Jersey, Maryland, Virginia, and Saint Georges, Grenada

Caption: Harris and Agee allegedly coordinated the finance of the firearms trafficking scheme through Whitaker and Young.

“When bad guys buy guns here and ship them up to our nation’s beautiful capital to foment unrest and mayhem, they threaten the safety of families and communities who live there, along with all of the eager citizens, families and kids, who save up to make the trip and visit the patriotic history and grandeur.” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle. “Working with ATF and our law enforcement partners, we will continue to aggressively investigate these schemes and prosecute those who violate federal law. If you are making sham purchases to illegally run guns in Eastern North Carolina, we will find you and prosecute you.”

“This operation exemplifies the commitment of our federal, state, and local partners working together under the Make DC Safe and Beautiful initiative,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Gun‑running networks do not respect state lines, and neither does our determination to stop them. This joint effort shows how coordinated enforcement can protect both Washington, D.C. communities and the communities where these schemes originate.”

“If you traffic firearms to violent criminals, gang members, or prohibited persons, ATF will find you and hold you accountable,” said ATF Director Rob Cekada. “Working with our partners on the D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force, we are dismantling trafficking networks and stopping the violence they fuel in our nation’s capital. State lines will not protect you.”

“The statistics show that the D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force is making a real difference in reducing crime,” said Associate Director of Operations for the United States Marshals Service Aaron Sawyer. “With every arrest we make and every illegal firearm we seize, we are helping prevent future crimes and protect people from becoming victims. That is the impact of this operation that can sometimes get lost in the numbers. Fewer crimes mean fewer victims and safer communities for everyone.”

The indictment charges the following individuals, including two defendants — Arnise Lecresha Young and Antonique Whitaker — who hold valid Special Police Officer licenses in the District of Columbia:

  • Brian “B” Agee, 40, with one count of conspiracy to traffic firearms in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 933(a)(2) and (a)(3), six counts of firearms trafficking and aiding and abetting in violation of 18 U.S.C. §§ 933(a)(2) and 2, and six counts of aiding and abetting the making of a false statement to a federally licensed firearms dealer in violation of 18 U.S.C. §§ 922(a)(6), 924(a)(2), and 2. 
  • Arnise Lecresha Young, 33, with one count of conspiracy to traffic firearms in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 933(a)(2) and (a)(3), six counts of aiding and abetting firearms trafficking in violation of 18 U.S.C. §§ 933(a)(2) and 2, and six counts of aiding and abetting the making of a false statement to a federally licensed firearms dealer.
  • Frank “Fatboy” Rayvone Harris, 38, with one count of conspiracy to traffic firearms in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 933(a)(2) and (a)(3).
  • Antonique Whitaker, 34, with one count of conspiracy to traffic firearms in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 933(a)(2) and (a)(3), two counts of aiding and abetting firearms trafficking in violation of 18 U.S.C. §§ 933(a)(2) and 2, and two counts of aiding and abetting the making of a false statement to a federally licensed firearms dealer in violation of 18 U.S.C. §§ 922(a)(6), 924(a)(2), and 2.
  • Christian Shedetta Atkinson, 30, with one count of conspiracy to traffic firearms in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 933(a)(2) and (a)(3), and with one count of making a false statement to a federally licensed firearms dealer in violation of 18 U.S.C. §§ 922(a)(6) and 924(a)(2).

If convicted, the defendants face a maximum penalty of 15 years in federal prison for conspiracy to traffic firearms and firearms trafficking offenses, and 10 years in federal prison for offenses involving false statements to federally licensed firearms dealers. Any sentence would be determined by a federal district court judge after consideration of the applicable sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors.

Press Conference on Federal Charges Stemming from a Joint Firearms-Trafficking Enforcement Operation 

Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina and Jeanine Ferris Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia made the announcement. The ATF is investigating the case.

A copy of this press release is located on our website. Related court documents and information are located on the website of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina or on PACER by searching for Case No. 5:26-CR-218.

An indictment is merely an accusation. The defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty

PHOENIX, Ariz. - The Department of Justice and FBI announced today results of the personnel surge in support of Operation Not Forgotten 2026, which focuses on unresolved cases in Indian country with a priority on cases involving violence against women and children, including those who are missing or murdered.

In its fourth year, Operation Not Forgotten surged personnel and investigative resources across the country from April 1 through September 30, resulting in 118 arrests, 41 individuals charged federally, 25 child victims identified or located, and 72 weapons recovered. FBI agents conducted 990 interviews and 232 search operations. Arrests increased by 123% and subjects charged by 52% over 2025.

“Operation Not Forgotten and Operation Steadfast Promise are signposts of the commitment the Department of Justice has made to our tribal partners,” said U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine. “We are in this fight right alongside you – the fight for answers, the fight for safety, and the fight for justice.” 

FBI’s Operation Steadfast Promise

Operation Steadfast Promise, first announced in 2026, is a continuing comprehensive surge of resources to address a wide range of violent criminal threats impacting Indian country. Operation Steadfast Promise builds on the successes of Operation Not Forgotten with the addition of multiple new initiatives to improve public safety in Tribal communities. The FBI, in coordination with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices, the Bureau of Indian Affairs Missing and Murdered Unit, Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and Tribal and other federal law enforcement partners, is working across multiple territories to bring investigative aid to cases and resolution for victims and their families. Since Operation Steadfast Promise began in April, the FBI opened over 1,200 new investigations in Indian country, obtained criminal charges on 678 subjects, made over 700 arrests, recovered 2,260 weapons, and made 140 drug seizures.

This year, Operation Not Forgotten continued to address the over 4,000 open investigations in Indian country including death investigations, child abuse cases, domestic violence, and adult sexual abuse investigations, underscoring the persistent and urgent need for sustained resource investment in these communities. 

During Operation Not Forgotten, the FBI surged personnel, including investigative, intelligence, and other support personnel, on rotating temporary duty assignments across Indian country in twelve FBI field offices, in Albuquerque, Billings, Detroit, Denver, Jackson, Las Vegas, Minneapolis, Oklahoma City, Omaha, Portland, Phoenix and Salt Lake City. Working in close coordination with Tribal law enforcement agencies, the BIA Missing and Murdered Unit, and U.S. Attorneys' Offices, together law enforcement worked to advance open investigations and pursue accountability for victims and their families.

A few examples of cases prosecuted by the District of Arizona during this period include:

U.S. v. Duane King, et al. – On Aug. 18, a federal grand jury indicted Duane King and Karrah King for Aiding and Abetting Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury and Aiding and Abetting Assault Resulting in Substantial Bodily Injury of an Intimate Partner. According to court documents, on July 26, the victim was waiting in a car at a gas station on the Navajo Nation when Duane King and Karrah King approached the vehicle. Duane King smashed the back windows with an axe, dragged the victim from the vehicle, and kicked the victim repeatedly, resulting in serious injury. On Oct. 8, Karrah King pleaded guilty to simple assault. She was sentenced to three years of probation. Duane King is currently scheduled for trial on Jan. 5, 2027.

U.S. v. James Junior Kenneth – On Sep. 9, a federal grand jury indicted Kenneth with Arson and Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury. According to court documents, Kenneth set fire to his mother’s home in Teec Nos Pos, Arizona on the Navajo Nation on Aug. 21. Later that same day, Kenneth assaulted another family member by striking them repeatedly in the head, causing serious injury. Kenneth was arrested on Aug. 31 and remains in custody. Trial is currently scheduled for Feb. 2, 2027.

U.S. v. Franlando Camarillo Carroll – On Sep. 29, a federal grand jury indicted Carroll for Aggravated Sexual Abuse of a Child. According to court documents, Carroll sexually abused a female child under the age of 12 earlier this year on the Navajo Nation. The case is pending. 

U.S. v. Jacob Ferlando Nosie - On Aug. 25, a federal grand jury indicted Nosie for Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury and Assault with a Dangerous Weapon. Nosie is alleged to have stabbed a family member after an argument on July 9. The assault took place on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation and resulted in the victim suffering significant, life-threatening injuries. The case is still pending arrest. 

The national release on Operation Not Forgotten can be found here.

Additionally, the FBI has brought focus to a new FBI’s Voices Not Forgotten webpage that includes a searchable and interactive map that brings attention to FBI investigations in Indian country where the FBI, in coordination with state, local and Tribal law enforcement are seeking the public’s assistance. In August 2026, the FBI announced the establishment of a new protocol which created a minimum reward of up to $25,000 for all publicly advertised cases involving homicides, kidnappings and missing persons in Indian country where the FBI has assumed jurisdiction.

The FBI remains committed to standing alongside Tribal communities, federal partners, and local law enforcement to address the violent crime threats that continue to impact Indian country. To learn more, visit fbi.gov/investigate/violent-crime/indian-country-crime.

The FBI encourages anyone with information related to unresolved violent crimes in Indian country to contact their local FBI field office or submit a tip at tips.fbi.gov.

CASE NUMBERS: 26-CR-08133-PCT-SMM (King); 26-CR-08158-PCT-DJH (Kenneth); 26-CR-08174-PCT-SHD (Carroll); 26-CR-08143-PCT (Nosie)
RELEASE NUMBER: 2026-179_Operation Not Forgotten

# # #

For more information on the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, visit http://www.justice.gov/usao/az/
Follow the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, on Twitter @USAO_AZ for the latest news.

ALEXANDRIA, Va. – Learning Care Group, Inc. (LCG) paid a civil penalty of $50,000 to the United States, $12,000 in compensatory damages to an individual complainant, and agreed to additional remedial actions to settle allegations that LCG, by and through a La Petite Academy located in Chesapeake (La Petite Academy–Taylor Road), violated Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

LCG operates a nationwide network of more than 1,150 schools, and under eleven brands: La Petite Academy, Inc.; Childtime; Tutor Time; The Children's Courtyard; Everbrook Academy; Montessori Unlimited; AppleTree & Gilden Woods; U-GRO; Creative Kids Learning Center; Young School; and Pathways Learning Academy.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia opened an investigation after receiving a complaint alleging that La Petite Academy-Taylor Road refused to enroll the complainant’s child in their afterschool program because of the child’s mobility disability and associated use of a wheelchair. As part of the investigation of this complaint, the U.S. Department of Justice’s Fair Housing Testing Program conducted testing, which refers to the use of individuals who, without any intent to patronize a particular place of public accommodation or partake in a given service, make inquiries at that place for the purpose of gathering information. 

As a result of the investigation, the United States alleged that LCG, by and through La Petite Academy-Taylor Road, violated the ADA by discriminating against the complainant and the complainant’s child by denying the child the opportunity to participate in and benefit from La Petite Academy-Taylor Road’s services because the child required the use of a wheelchair due to a mobility disability. 

The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Virginia and the U.S. Department of Justice’s Fair Housing Testing Program and Disability Rights Section. 

The matter was investigated by Assistant U.S. Attorney David Tannenbaum. 

For more information on the ADA, visit www.ada.gov or call the Department of Justice’s toll-free ADA Information Line at (800) 514-0301 (Voice) or (833) 610-1264 (TTY). Accessibility specialists are available to answer questions from individuals, businesses, and state or local governments. All calls are confidential.

A copy of this press release may be found on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia.

The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division), the Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the USDA Office of Inspector General today announced a nationwide series of enforcement actions targeting fraud involving the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and related USDA programs.

Between Sept. 1, and today, the Fraud Division, 13 U.S. Attorneys’ Offices, and the Utah Attorney General’s Office conducted the Department’s first National USDA Benefits and Program Fraud Enforcement Surge. This coordinated effort resulted in actions against more than 40 defendants whose alleged or proven schemes caused nearly $45 million in intended losses to the federal government. Nearly $42 million of that amount involved fraud against SNAP benefits, which provide monthly food assistance to low-income individuals and families. Another case involved attempted fraud against a USDA crop‑insurance program designed to help farmers recover from covered losses.

“These schemes siphoned millions from taxpayers and robbed struggling Americans of the benefits they depend on so fraudsters could use them for their own selfish purposes,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Through our partnership with the Department of Agriculture, this nationwide surge exposed and disrupted criminal networks that targeted vulnerable American families. The Department of Justice will continue working to root out fraud in every federal agency and program.”

“Every instance of SNAP fraud has two victims: families in dire need and taxpayers. Today, we are reminding fraudsters that we will find you and prosecute you to the fullest extent of the law,” said Secretary Brooke Rollins of USDA. “Thank you to USDA’s OIG and our state and federal partners for working with us to bring justice to families harmed by criminals. Under the Trump Administration, food stamp fraud ends now.”

“The human cost of these fraud schemes is measured not in spreadsheets, but in the panic of a mother whose card is declined and the hunger her children endure because someone hijacked their benefits,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “These schemes inflict real harm on real American families, and they erode the trust taxpayers place in programs designed to keep Americans fed. That is why the Fraud Division is acting with urgency, not just to prosecute fraud, but to protect the people who depend on these lifelines.”

“SNAP fraud despicably robs from low-income Americans that rely on the program for food assistance and diverts taxpayer funds to line the pockets of fraudsters and bankroll other criminal activities like guns and drugs that make American communities less safe,” said Inspector General John Walk of USDA OIG. “No more! USDA OIG is committed to support Vice President Vance’s leadership to disrupt fraud schemes and send criminals straight to prison.  I am honored to stand with Vice President Vance today and grateful for our special agents whose work as part of this nationwide surge brought significant law enforcement actions against fraudsters in dozens of cases across the country.  This surge is only the beginning. USDA OIG will continue to unite behind our partners in the whole-of-government fight to eliminate fraud and hold fraudsters to account.”

“SNAP benefit fraud steals from American taxpayers and from the families who depend on these benefits to put food on the table”, said Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon of the Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). “Homeland Security Investigations is working closely with our law enforcement and prosecutorial partners to identify and dismantle the criminal networks that use skimming devices, stolen identities, fraudulent retailers, and other schemes to exploit this critical program. Those who profit by stealing public benefits should know that HSI will pursue the evidence, follow the money, and hold them accountable.”

Nationwide SNAP Benefit Fraud Enforcement Surge

SNAP fraud harms vulnerable families who rely on these benefits to buy food. One recent victim, a mother whose electronic benefit transfer (EBT) card was compromised, discovered her benefits had been stolen only when her card was declined at a grocery store. She was forced to take out loans to feed her children and reported significant anxiety and depression as a result.

Mother of four reports being forced to take out a loan after her EBT card was compromised.

Notable cases

  1. [Indictment]  United States v. Jorag Yaseen and Rami Kanaan, Southern District of Ohio Case No. 3:26-cr-00099-TMR — $29.7 million intended Loss
  • A federal grand jury indicted Jorag Yaseen and Rami Kanaan on charges related to an alleged scheme to defraud the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) through fraudulent electronic benefit transfer (EBT) transactions. According to the indictment, Yaseen and Kanaan operated approved retail food stores in Chicago, Illinois. Prosecutors allege that, between approximately February 2024 and April 2025, the defendants and others processed thousands of transactions using stolen Ohio and other state EBT account information. The indictment alleges that the transactions falsely appeared to represent legitimate purchases of authorized food products, even though no bona fide sales occurred. The alleged transactions generated interstate wire communications between Illinois and servers associated with Ohio’s SNAP administration. Prosecutors further allege that the scheme caused state administrators to transfer millions of dollars in federal funds to accounts controlled by the defendants and others, resulting in an estimated loss of approximately $29.7 million to the United States. The indictment also alleges that some of the proceeds were used to purchase automobiles for use and shipment overseas. Yaseen and Kanaan are charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to commit money laundering. The indictment identifies three alleged interstate wire transactions on March 4, 2024, involving a stolen Ohio EBT card associated with a Greene County resident and totaling $1,243.46.

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys/Fraud Division Deputy Chiefs Ryan Saunders and Brian McDonough for the Southern District of Ohio.

  1. [Indictment] United States v. Mercedes New, Northern District of Georgia (26-CR-473) — $4.4 million intended loss 
  • On October 7, a federal grand jury indicted rapper and social media influencer Mercedes New, otherwise known as Shawty Dred, for criminal food stamp fraud, mail fraud, access device fraud, and aggravated identity theft. The investigation began in 2025, when the Georgia Department of Human Services Office of Inspector General determined there was an attack on the interactive voice response (IVR) system used by SNAP benefit recipients. Specifically, they determined that phone numbers associated with Mercedes New contacted the SNAP EBT IVR over 9,000 times, accessing over 350 separate SNAP accounts. The transaction total for SNAP benefit cards connected to Mercedes New at that time were estimated at $1.8 million. Of that $1.8 million, GADHS-OIG determined that approximately $635,000 were transactions at Shawty Dred LLC in Atlanta, GA, a previously SNAP authorized retail store owned by Mercedes New. Additionally, in November 2025, Mercedes New was arrested at Walmart in East Point, GA for soliciting customers to buy SNAP EBT cards from him.  At the time of his arrest, East Point Police Department seized 14 Georgia EBT cards. These 14 EBT cards accounted for over 350 of the calls made to the IVR from the same number listed as the store phone number for Shawty Dred LLC in his SNAP retailer application. Ultimately, the investigation discovered that more than 500 Georgia EBT cards are linked to New, with an estimated fraud loss amount of $4.4 million in stolen benefits. New was arrested in Las Vegas, NV on October 13.

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Tracia King for the Northern District of Georgia with assistance from District Fraud Counsel AOR: Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas Joy for the Northern District of Georgia.

  1. [Guilty Plea] United States v. Mark Frisbie, Middle District of Florida (No. 2:26-cr-00251-SPC-NPM) — $3.2 million actual loss
  • On September 29, defendant Mark Frisbie pleaded guilty to submitting a false crop-insurance claim. As part of his guilty plea, Frisbie admitted that — from 2019 to 2024 — he knowingly signed and certified numerous false crop-insurance claims that underreported his actual crop production.  The underreporting of Frisbie’s actual crop production caused the federal government to pay more than $1.7 million in crop-insurance indemnities that it otherwise would not have paid.  As part of his guilty plea, Frisbie acknowledged that he actually grew and sold more than $6.8 million bell peppers and tomatoes during relevant times — but that he only reported (for crop-insurance purposes) sales of less than $800,000.  In other words, Frisbie fraudulently concealed more than $6 million in crop sales.  Based on his false representations in his crop-insurance claims, Frisbie caused the federal government to pay $1,748,408 in crop insurance indemnities that it otherwise would not have paid.  In addition to admitting to submitting false crop-insurance claims, Frisbie admitted to defrauding two other federal government programs designed to benefit farmers — namely, the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program and the Emergency Relief Program.  Frisbie has agreed to pay $1,506,992.26 in restitution to the Farm Service Agency based on his fraud against these taxpayer-funded farmer-relief programs. 

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Chelsey Hanson and Simon Eth for the Middle District of Florida, with assistance from. District Fraud Counsel AOR: Assistant U.S. Attorney Jay Trezevant for the Middle District of Florida. 

  1. [Sentencing]:  United States v. Dumitru, et al., District of Oregon (No. 3:24-cr-00383-AN) — $4.4 million intended loss 
  • On September 9, Ana Patricia Escalante, the leader of a transport crew that crisscrossed the country collecting and shipping infant formula purchased with stolen food benefits, was sentenced to 27 months in federal prison and ordered to pay $2.4 million in restitution. Escalante was one of 17 defendants indicted in Oregon in October 2024 in connection with an interstate conspiracy involving more than $2.4 million in stolen SNAP benefits. To date, 12 defendants have been sentenced in the case, receiving a combined 157 months in prison and orders to pay full restitution. According to court documents, members of the conspiracy obtained SNAP account information through skimming devices and other means and used the stolen benefits to purchase massive quantities of infant formula and other food products from stores in Oregon, Washington, California, and other states. Members of the theft crew, most of whom were Romanian nationals unlawfully present in the United States, sold fraudulently obtained merchandise to Escalante and her transport crew. The scheme depleted benefits belonging to thousands of low-income families nationwide, leaving victims—including parents and seniors—unable to purchase groceries. Escalante’s transport crew collected the merchandise, stockpiled it at residences and storage units, and transported it in private vehicles and through commercial carriers for resale on the black market. Commercial shipping records documented more than 124,000 pounds of infant formula shipped from the conspiracy’s storage facilities, with an estimated value exceeding $2.4 million.

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Nicholas Meyers and Geoff Garrow for the District of Oregon with assistance from. District Fraud Counsel AOR: Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas Meyers for the District of Oregon.

  1. [Guilty Plea + Sentencing]: United States v. Kirk Deshaun Woodley and United States v. Chantel LaShawn Peavy, Eastern District of Michigan (Nos. 2:26-cr-20191 and 2:25-cr-20834) —$1.1. million in intended loss
  • Kirk Deshaun Woodley conspired with Chantel LaShawn Peavy and others to submit hundreds of fraudulent applications for SNAP benefits by obtaining and using the names and personal identifying information of more than 650 individual victims.  Once the applications were approved, the funds were loaded on to EBT cards, and the cards were mailed to addresses controlled by Woodley and Peavy, who then either sold the cards to other co-conspirators for resale or accessed the SNAP benefits themselves by making purchases with the cards.

Woodley pleaded guilty to Conspiracy to Commit Wire Fraud and Aggravated Identity Theft on September 22; Peavy was sentenced on the conspiracy to 18 months imprisonment on October 20.

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Corinne M. Lambert for the Eastern District of Michigan with assistance from . District Fraud Counsel AOR: Assistant U.S. Attorney Jason Norwood for the Eastern District of Michigan.

  1. [Indictment]  United States v. Mohinder Singh, Western District of Michigan (No. 1:26-cr-00094-JMB) — $1,089,949 in intended loss
  • Mohinder Singh, the owner/operator of a convenience store in Lansing, Michigan, was charged by a grand jury with theft or conversion of public money and nine counts of SNAP benefits fraud. The indictment alleges that Singh unlawfully exchanged cash and other ineligible items for SNAP benefits with his customers and allowed some customers to use SNAP benefits to pay debts owed to him. Singh typically provided SNAP recipients with an exchange rate of $0.50 in U.S. currency per $1 of SNAP benefits transferred, according to the indictment. Additionally, it is alleged that Singh charged a fee payable in SNAP benefits after extending credit to some of his customers.

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney/District Fraud Counsel Christopher O'Connor for the Western District of Michigan. 

  1. [Complaint] United States v. Sqar Qahtan et al., Northern District of Ohio (No. 1:26-mj-3194-RJS) — $1 million in intended loss
  • On Oct. 6, Sqar Qahtan, 31, Baligh Naji, 34, Ahmed Al Hamami, 36, all citizens of Yemen residing in Euclid, Ohio, along with Mohsin Mohsin, 28, of Syracuse, New York; Mariah Hatcher, 30, of Euclid, Ohio, and Almotawakil Nassr, 29, of Detroit, Michigan, were charged in criminal complaints with SNAP Benefits Fraud, Wire Fraud, and Conspiracy to Commit Wire Fraud.  For approximately two years, the defendants allegedly operated a conspiracy to exchange Ohio SNAP benefit cards for cash, marijuana, and other non-SNAP items while employed at a gas station convenience store in Euclid, Ohio. The larger conspiracy is estimated to have fraudulently obtained more than $1 million in food stamp benefits.

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Erica Barnhill for the Northern District of Ohio with assistance from District Fraud Counsel AOR: Deputy Chief Assistant U.S. Attorney Brian McDonough for the Northern District of Ohio.

  1. [Complaint] United States v. Rodolfo Armando Fernandez Guzman, District of Massachusetts (No. 1:26-mj-03349-JDH) — $22,402 in intended loss
  • As alleged in charging documents, Fernandez Guzman is a Dominican national that stole the identity of a U.S. citizen to fraudulently obtain $22,402 in SNAP benefits, $98,481.25 in MassHealth benefits, and $45,596 in Section 8 housing benefits. In addition, Fernandez Guzman allegedly obtained two state ID cards, a learner's permit, and three driver's licenses in Massachusetts and Arizona using the stolen identity. The Complaint further alleges that Fernandez Guzman was convicted of two felonies in Arizona and received prison sentences under the victim's identity.

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney James Nagelberg for the District of Massachusetts. District Fraud Counsel AOR: Assistant U.S. Attorney James Nagelberg District of Massachusetts.

  1. [Indictment]  United States v. Michael Swanson, et al., Eastern District of Pennsylvania — $13,392 in intended loss
  • On October 8, a 39-count indictment of Michael Swanson, Nicole Swanson, David Dziobczynski and Caitlyn Eusden Swanson, was filed. On October 14, all three Swansons and Dziobczynski were arrested. Charges include Wire Fraud, Mail Fraud, Kidnapping, Transportation of Individuals for Illicit Sexual Activity, False Statements, Social Security Fraud, Theft of Government Funds, SNAP Fraud and Cyberstalking. The Swansons groomed, lured, and enticed intellectually disabled women to live with them for the purpose of controlling their Social Security and SNAP benefits. Michael Swanson also engaged in sexual acts with the women, to which they lacked the capacity to consent. The estimated fraud loss is $13,392 to SNAP and $27,227 to the Social Security Administration. All defendants were arrested on October 14.

Prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Megan Curran for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania with assistance from. District Fraud Counsel AOR: Assistant U.S. Attorney Meghan Bisio for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

  1. [Information]  State of Utah v. Besmulla Yaqoobi — $5,994.89 in intended loss
  • In 2022, Defendant co-owned a store, Sahara Market, located in Taylorsville, Utah. On November 8, 2022, Defendant’s co-owner signed a U.S. Department of Agriculture Food and Nutritional Services (FNS) contract on behalf of the Sahara Market. The FNS Contract specifically stated that it was prohibited to trade cash in exchange for SNAP benefits and doing so would be a violation of SNAP regulations. The USDA-OIG began a joint investigation with the Taylorsville Police Department into the Sahara Market in 2023. Between January 2024 and April 2024, surveillance was conducted on the Sahara Market. Surveillance revealed 15-20 individuals that entered the market, made large EBT transactions, and subsequently exited the market shortly after with little to no items. Transactions from these instances totaled $5,429.89. Similar transactions occurred on July 8, 2024, and Aug. 8, 2024.

HOUSTON – A 53-year-old Guatemalan national has been ordered to federal prison following his third conviction for illegally reentering the country. 

Hector Alexander Cabrera pleaded guilty July 27.

U.S. District Judge George C. Hanks ordered Cabrera to serve 63 months in federal prison. As an illegal alien, he is expected to face removal proceedings following his imprisonment.

Cabrera has two prior convictions for illegal reentry, as well as convictions for unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, evading arrest or detention, criminal mischief, burglary of a vehicle, theft, and assault.

Authorities first removed Cabrera from the United States in September 2006. Despite multiple subsequent removals, he continued to return illegally.

On Aug. 19, 2024, law enforcement again discovered Cabrera in Houston without authorization to be in the United States.

Cabrera has been and will remain in custody pending transfer to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility to be determined in the near future.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement - Enforcement and Removal Operations conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Ekua Assabill prosecuted the case. 

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations, and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

results.body:
DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that an illegal alien from Mexico with a significant U.S. criminal history was convicted on Oct. 16, for stealing the identity of a deceased U.S. citizen and fraudulently obtaining a U.S. passport.

In October 2024, a federal grand jury indicted Vidal Blanco-Blas, 62, for false statement in application and use of United States Passport and aggravated identity theft. After a three-day trial and approximately two hours of deliberation, a jury convicted him on both counts.

“Exploiting the identity of a deceased American infant to sneak into the U.S and conceal a decades-long life of crime and fraud is an appalling act that undermines the integrity of our immigration system and erodes trust in our nation’s most vital security documents,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Identity fraud of this magnitude endangers national security, and this office will aggressively pursue anyone who seeks to manipulate our systems or compromise the security of the United States.” 

“Diplomatic Security Service Special Agents are tasked with preserving the sanctity of national security documents like the United States passport,” said Diplomatic Security Service Houston Field Office Special Agent in Charge Ryan Pack. “In support of our mission and authorities delegated by the U.S. Secretary of State, our cadre will continue to tirelessly work to identify and bring forth to prosecution any party attempting to undermine the most trusted identity document in the world.” 

According to evidence presented at trial, Blanco-Blas entered the U.S. over 40 years ago, using the stolen identity of a deceased United States Citizen, Julio Cesar Torres—an infant who passed away in Mexico at approximately 3 months old. Once in the U.S, Blanco-Blas utilized the infant’s identity to illegally obtain a Social Security number, State of Texas driver’s license, voter registration card and U.S. passport. 

Blanco-Blas has significant criminal history in the U.S. He was previously convicted and sentenced to 84 months for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute a controlled substance, 120 months for possession of marijuana, and 21 months for possession with intent to distribute up to 30 kilograms of marijuana under his stolen identity. 

Witnesses at trial testified that Blanco-Blas held himself out to be Julio Cesar Torres, going so far as to instruct his daughter to sustain the charade that he was her “uncle,” Julio Cesar Torres, when in public. This charade continued until April 11, 2023, when Vidal Blanco-Blas submitted an application to renew his fraudulently obtained United States Passport in Greenville, Texas. Due to advancements in investigative techniques, the United States Department of State learned of the passport fraud and discovered the fraudster’s true identity. 

Blanco-Blas faces up to 12 years in federal prison. His sentencing date is set for March 22, 2027, before U.S. District Judge Sam A. Lindsay. 

The United States Department of State, Diplomatic Security Service conducted the investigation with assistance from the Social Security Administration, Office of Inspector General and the United States Department of State, Bureau of Consular Affairs, National Passport Center. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Luis A. Suarez and Ashley Koos from the Narcotics Section are prosecuting the case.

Alexandria, Va. – Securiport Limited Liability Company (Securiport) and Alex Stewart International, LLC (ASI), have agreed to pay a combined $1,816,943 to settle civil False Claims Act allegations arising from the submission of statements on their applications for so-called Second Draw Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans.
The United States alleged that Securiport and ASI received Second Draw PPP loans, which were later forgiven, after submitting false statements on loan applications that they, together with affiliates, had no more than 300 employees, an eligibility requirement specific to Second Draw PPP loans. Based on that purported false statement, the United States alleged that Securiport and ASI falsely certified they were eligible.
The settlement began with a lawsuit, United States ex rel. Verity Investigations, LLC v. Securiport Limited Liability Company, No. 1:25-cv-2027 , filed under the whistleblower provision of the False Claims Act, which permits private parties to file suit on behalf of the United States for false claims presented to the federal government. The whistleblower received 10% of the government’s recovery. The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia and the U.S. Small Business Administration.
The matter was investigated by Assistant U.S. Attorney David Tannenbaum.

The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division), the Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the USDA Office of Inspector General today announced a nationwide series of enforcement actions targeting fraud involving the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and related USDA programs.
Between Sept. 1, and today, the Fraud Division, 13 U.S. Attorneys’ Offices, and the Utah Attorney General’s Office conducted the Department’s first National USDA Benefits and Program Fraud Enforcement Surge. This coordinated effort resulted in actions against more than 40 defendants whose alleged or proven schemes caused nearly $45 million in intended losses to the federal government. Nearly $42 million of that amount involved fraud against SNAP benefits, which provide monthly food assistance to low-income individuals and families. Another case involved attempted fraud against a USDA crop‑insurance program designed to help farmers recover from covered losses.
“These schemes siphoned millions from taxpayers and robbed struggling Americans of the benefits they depend on so fraudsters could use them for their own selfish purposes,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Through our partnership with the Department of Agriculture, this nationwide surge exposed and disrupted criminal networks that targeted vulnerable American families. The Department of Justice will continue working to root out fraud in every federal agency and program.”

False Claims Act; Paycheck Protection Program

TOLEDO, Ohio – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio announced today that Murotech Ohio Corporation, an automotive component parts manufacturer with its principal place of business in St. Marys, Ohio, has agreed to pay $3,039,615, of which $1,085,577 is restitution, to resolve allegations under the False Claims Act (FCA) that it knowingly provided false information to obtain Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans and loan forgiveness. The company is a subsidiary of Muro Corporation, located in Japan.
The PPP program was launched through the Small Business Administration (SBA) to provide eligible companies with financial support during the COVID-19 pandemic. Murotech Ohio’s first application submitted in May 2020 certified that the company had fewer than 500 employees, but in fact, it exceeded that amount when counting affiliates. A second application submitted in January of 2021 certified that it employed fewer than 300 employees, but in truth, the company employed far more when including affiliates. Murotech Ohio then applied to have both federal loans forgiven and certified on its submitted applications that the number of employees was below program limit requirements.

PHOENIX, Ariz. - The Department of Justice and FBI announced today results of the personnel surge in support of Operation Not Forgotten 2026, which focuses on unresolved cases in Indian country with a priority on cases involving violence against women and children, including those who are missing or murdered.
In its fourth year, Operation Not Forgotten surged personnel and investigative resources across the country from April 1 through September 30, resulting in 118 arrests, 41 individuals charged federally, 25 child victims identified or located, and 72 weapons recovered. FBI agents conducted 990 interviews and 232 search operations. Arrests increased by 123% and subjects charged by 52% over 2025.
“Operation Not Forgotten and Operation Steadfast Promise are signposts of the commitment the Department of Justice has made to our tribal partners,” said U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine. “We are in this fight right alongside you – the fight for answers, the fight for safety, and the fight for justice.”
FBI’s Operation Steadfast Promise
Operation Steadfast Promise, first announced in 2026, is a continuing comprehensive surge of resources to address a wide range of violent criminal threats impacting Indian country. Operation Steadfast Promise builds on the successes of Operation Not Forgotten with the addition of multiple new initiatives to improve public safety in Tribal communities.
